verdict.rationale: RevenueCat documents two API key types—public (limited) and secret (full server-side access with sensitive actions like refunds/promotional grants)—showing some credential separation (revenuecat-docs-5, revenuecat-docs-15, revenuecat-docs-19), and its MCP server/AI Toolkit let agents interact with the platform via these keys (revenuecat-docs-9, revenuecat-docs-17). However, there's no evidence of fine-grained, per-permission or read/write scoped key creation specifically intended for least-privilege agent access beyond the binary public/secret split. Missing for 10: documented ability to create custom-scoped/limited-permission API keys (e.g., read-only or feature-restricted) explicitly for AI agents, and any agent-specific credential management or rotation controls.
